mainTopic: The 'to you, and after you to so-and-so' gift: the first recipient's power to sell, deathbed gifts, and an אתרוג given this way
overview: The גמרא shows that the case of 'נכסי לך ואחריך לפלוני' is a מחלוקת between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about whether the first recipient may sell the property. A second ברייתא seems to flip both of their views. The גמרא resolves this. For רבי, one ruling is about the land itself and the other is about its produce. For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the first recipient should not sell לכתחילה, but a sale he already made stands דיעבד. אביי calls anyone who advises such a sale a 'cunning wicked person.' רבי יוחנן rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, except that a מתנת שכיב מרע by the first recipient does nothing, because it takes effect only after death and the second recipient's right comes first. A משנה about a גט 'if I die' proves that אביי held this 'after death' view. רבי יוחנן's ruling also covers freeing slaves and making shrouds. Finally, רב נחמן בר רב חסדא applies the מחלוקת to an אתרוג given 'to you, and after you,' and רב נחמן בר יצחק begins to challenge him; his challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The question depends on a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the issue is a מחלוקת תנאים. It quotes a ברייתא: רבי says the second recipient takes the property back from the buyers, while רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the second gets only what the first left over.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים. A ברייתא teaches: if someone said 'My property is yours, and after you it goes to so-and-so,' and the first person went ahead, sold it and used up the money, then the second person takes it back from the buyers. That is רבי's view. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the second person gets only what the first one left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question it just asked by showing that תנאים already argued about it in a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case of 'נכסי לך ואחריך לפלוני,' the first person sold the property. רבי holds the sale does not hold against the second recipient, so the second can take the land back from the buyers. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds the sale stands, so the second gets only what remains unsold.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
And after you, to so-and-so (the second recipient)
Takes the property back from the buyers

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the two basic positions on how much power the first recipient has in an אחריך gift.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of tanna'im.
As it is taught: 'My property is to you, and after you to so-and-so,'
and the first one went in, sold it, and consumed the proceeds –
the second one takes it out of the buyers' hands,
these are the words of Rabbi.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לַשֵּׁנִי אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁשִּׁיֵּיר רִאשׁוֹן.
phrases.english: The second has only what the first left over.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised just before this part of the daf.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question is a מחלוקת between רבי, who says the second recipient takes the land back from the buyers, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who says the second gets only what is left.

steps.title: A second ברייתא where the opinions seem reversed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another ברייתא. Here רבי says the first recipient may sell, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the first may only eat the produce. This looks like the opposite of the first ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא points out a contradiction. Another ברייתא says: 'My property is yours, and after you to so-and-so.' The first person may go in, sell, and use the money. That is רבי's view. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the first person has only the right to eat the produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a contradiction. It quotes a second ברייתא and will point out the problem in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first ברייתא, רבי limited the first recipient, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל let the sale stand. Here it is the other way around. רבי lets the first recipient sell, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל limits him to the produce.

keyTerms.meaning: And they pointed out a contradiction
The right to eat or use the produce, not the land itself

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
'My property is to you, and after you to so-and-so' –
the first may go in, sell, and consume,
these are the words of Rabbi.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לָרִאשׁוֹן אֶלָּא אֲכִילַת פֵּירוֹת בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: The first has only the eating of the produce alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that seems to contradict both opinions in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The positions of רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל as stated in the first ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא gives each תנא the opposite position.

steps.title: Each תנא contradicts himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states the problem outright: רבי contradicts רבי, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל contradicts רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difficulty: רבי contradicts himself, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל contradicts himself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the double contradiction between the two ברייתות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי said the second recipient takes the land from the buyers, yet he also said the first may sell. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said the first's sale stands, yet he also said the first has only the produce. Each תנא needs his own answer.

keyTerms.meaning: One statement of רבי against another statement of רבי

phrases.english: There is a difficulty: Rabbi against Rabbi,

phrases.aramaic: וּדְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אַדְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל!
phrases.english: and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel against Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the contradiction set up in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: Both תנאים's consistency across the two ברייתות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same תנא cannot both allow and forbid the first recipient's sale.

steps.title: רבי: land itself versus produce
steps.stepSummary: רבי's two rulings deal with different things. The first recipient cannot sell the land itself, but he may sell the produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי against רבי is not a problem. One ruling is about the land itself, and the other is about the produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves רבי's contradiction by saying each ברייתא talks about something different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When רבי says the second recipient takes the land back from buyers, he means the land itself (גופא). When he says the first may sell and use the money, he means the produce (פירא). So the two rulings fit together.

phrases.english: Rabbi against Rabbi is not difficult –
this is regarding the property itself, that is regarding the produce.
phrases.notes: The first ברייתא, where the buyers lose the land, is about the land. The second, where he may sell, is about the produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half of the contradiction in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each ruling refers to something different.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings seemed to be about selling the land itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי, the first recipient may sell the produce but not the land itself.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: from the start versus after the fact
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's two rulings are about different stages. לכתחילה, the first recipient should only use the produce. דיעבד, if he did sell, the sale stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל against רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is not a problem. One ruling is about what he may do from the start, and the other is about what happens after the fact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's contradiction by separating what is allowed from the start from what holds after the fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The first has only the produce' tells the first recipient what he should do לכתחילה. 'The second gets only what the first left over' tells us that if he already sold (דיעבד), the sale stands. So he should not sell, but if he does, it works.

keyTerms.meaning: After the fact, once it was already done

steps.whatToRemember: In the case of 'נכסי לך ואחריך לפלוני': for רבי, the first recipient may sell the produce but not the land itself. For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the first recipient should not sell the land, but if he does, the sale stands, and the second recipient gets only what is left.
steps.confusionAlert: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does not allow the first recipient to sell from the start. He only says that a sale already made is valid.

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אַדְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel against Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
is not difficult –
this is from the outset, that is after the fact.

steps.triggerLanguage: דרבן שמעון בן גמליאל אדרבן שמעון בן גמליאל לא קשיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second half of the contradiction in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing what is allowed from the start (לכתחילה) from what is valid after the fact (דיעבד).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His two rulings seemed to conflict about whether the sale is valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first recipient should only use the produce, but a sale he already made stands.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both תנאים are consistent once we see what each ruling refers to.

steps.title: אביי: Advising the first recipient to sell is cunning wickedness
steps.stepSummary: אביי calls anyone who advises the first recipient to sell the property, relying on רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, a 'cunning wicked person.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Who is a cunning wicked person? It is someone who advises selling the property, relying on the view of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a moral warning based on what we just learned in Step 5. Even though a sale works after the fact according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, advising someone to sell is wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said that according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the first recipient should not sell לכתחילה, but if he did, the sale stands. Someone who pushes him to sell is using a legal loophole to cheat the second recipient out of the property. Because he hides behind a technically valid ruling, he is called 'cunning' (ערום) and not just 'wicked.'

keyTerms.meaning: A cunning wicked person: someone who does wrong while staying technically within the law

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Who is a cunning wicked person?
This is one who gives advice
to sell the property
in line with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 5's distinction between לכתחילה and דיעבד in רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view, and adds a moral judgment against exploiting the דיעבד rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Advising the first recipient to sell, relying on the fact that the sale works after the fact, is cunning wickedness.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, except for a deathbed gift
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, but says רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agrees that giving the property away as a deathbed gift does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. And he agrees that if the first recipient gave the property away as a deathbed gift, he has done nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the practical הלכה: a sale by the first recipient stands after the fact. He then adds one exception, a gift given on one's deathbed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, if the first recipient transferred the property, the transfer works and the second gets only what is left. But a מתנת שכיב מרע, a gift by a dying person, is different. Even רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agrees it accomplishes nothing, and the second recipient still gets the property.

keyTerms.meaning: And he agrees (admits a case where he holds like the other view)
A gift given by a person on his deathbed
He has done nothing; the act has no effect

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halacha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.
And he agrees
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. Here he agrees that the second recipient wins.

phrases.english: that if he gave them away as a deathbed gift,
he has done nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the moral warning to the practical הלכה, and introduces an exception that the גמרא will now explain.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line for the case of 'to you, and after you to so-and-so.' The deathbed-gift exception becomes the focus of the next steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, but a transfer by the first recipient through a deathbed gift has no effect.

steps.title: Why doesn't a deathbed gift work?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the deathbed-gift exception.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a deathbed gift should be different from a regular sale. This short question sets up the next step, where אביי answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a sale by the first recipient works after the fact, why not a gift? The גמרא wants to know what makes a deathbed gift fail when other transfers succeed.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רבי יוחנן's exception in Step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a deathbed gift by the first recipient fails, when a sale by him would stand.

steps.title: אביי: A deathbed gift starts after death, and 'after you' comes first
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that a deathbed gift only takes effect after death, but the second recipient's right begins first, at the moment of death.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: A deathbed gift is acquired only after death, and the words 'after you' already came before it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question from Step 8. It is a matter of timing: the second recipient's right kicks in before the deathbed gift can take effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The property was given 'to you, and after you to so-and-so,' so the second recipient's right begins as soon as the first recipient dies. A deathbed gift only takes effect after the giver's death. By then, the property already belongs to the second recipient, so the deathbed gift has nothing to grab.

keyTerms.meaning: 'After you': the words giving the property to the second recipient

phrases.english: Abaye said:
A deathbed gift
is acquired only after death,
and 'after you' has already come before it.
phrases.notes: 'After you' means the second recipient's right, which starts the moment the first recipient dies.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מַתְּנַת שְׁכִיב מְרַע לֹא קָנָה אֶלָּא לְאַחַר מִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8's question with a timing argument.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A deathbed gift takes effect only after death, while the second recipient's right ('after you') begins at death, so the second recipient acquires first.

steps.title: Did אביי really say a deathbed gift takes effect after death?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: in a known dispute with רבא, אביי holds that a deathbed gift takes effect at the moment of death, not after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But did אביי really say this? Wasn't it stated: From when does a deathbed gift take effect? אביי said: at the moment death is completed. רבא said: after death is completed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that אביי's reason in Step 9 seems to clash with his own view in another dispute. There, he said a deathbed gift takes effect at the very moment of death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 9, אביי said the gift works only after death, which is why 'after you' wins. But in his argument with רבא, it is רבא who says 'after death.' אביי says 'with the completion of death,' meaning at the same moment. If the gift and the second recipient's right begin at the same instant, then 'after you' did not come first, and אביי's reason seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But did he really say this? (introduces a contradiction)
At the moment death is completed

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two views. In this dispute, רבא is the one who says 'after death.' אביי says 'at the moment of death.' That is exactly why his reason in Step 9 is being challenged.

phrases.english: But did Abaye really say this?
But wasn't it stated:
A deathbed gift: from when is it acquired?
Abaye said: at the moment death is completed,
and Rava said: after death is completed!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר אַבָּיֵי הָכִי? וְהָא אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in Step 9 by quoting a conflicting statement of אביי himself.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reason in Step 9, that a deathbed gift takes effect only after death.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In his dispute with רבא, אביי holds that a deathbed gift takes effect at the moment of death. If so, it begins at the same instant as the second recipient's right, so 'after you' did not come first.

steps.title: אביי took back his other statement
steps.stepSummary: The contradiction is solved by saying אביי retracted his view that a מתנת שכיב מרע takes effect at the moment of death.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי retracted that statement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from step 10. אביי changed his mind about one of his two statements.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9 אביי said a deathbed gift works only after death. Step 10 pointed out that in his dispute with רבא he said it works at the moment of death. The answer is that he dropped the 'moment of death' view, so his explanation in step 9 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: From that one, the other statement

phrases.english: Abaye retracted from that one.
phrases.notes: 'That one' is his view from the dispute with רבא, that a deathbed gift takes effect at the moment of death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction: one of the two conflicting statements was abandoned.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי holds two opposite views about when a deathbed gift takes effect.
steps.terutzMaskana: אביי retracted the 'moment of death' view, so his step 9 explanation stands.

steps.title: Maybe he took back the other statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know אביי retracted the 'moment of death' view and not his 'after death' view.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know he retracted that one? Maybe he retracted this one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. Maybe אביי dropped the 'after death' view instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'he retracted' fixes the contradiction, but it does not tell us which statement he dropped. If he dropped the 'after death' view, his explanation in step 9 falls apart. So the גמרא needs proof of which view he kept.

phrases.english: From where do we know that he retracted that one?
Perhaps he retracted this one!
phrases.notes: 'This one' is his statement in step 9, that a deathbed gift works only after death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 11 by asking which statement was retracted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that אביי retracted the 'moment of death' view.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The opposite retraction is just as possible, and it would undo אביי's explanation in step 9.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה about a divorce 'if I die'
steps.stepSummary: A משנה rules that a גט given 'if I die' or 'after death' does nothing. This shows deathbed instructions are meant for after death, so that is the view אביי kept.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't think that, for we learned: 'This is your גט if I die'; 'This is your גט from this illness'; 'This is your גט after death' — he has said nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves which view אביי kept by quoting a משנה from גיטין about a husband on his deathbed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats 'if I die' the same as 'after death', and in both cases the גט is worthless. So when a dying man says something should happen 'if I die', he means after death. That supports the 'after death' view, so אביי must have dropped the 'moment of death' view.

keyTerms.meaning: He has said nothing; it has no effect

phrases.english: That should not enter your mind, for we learned:
"This is your bill of divorce if I die";
"This is your bill of divorce from this illness";
"This is your bill of divorce after death" —
he has said nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 with a proof from a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That אביי kept the view that a deathbed gift takes effect only after death.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in גיטין: a גט given 'if I die' or 'after death' has no effect.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי's final view is that a deathbed gift takes effect after death. That explains why, according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the first recipient cannot give the property away as a deathbed gift: the second recipient's right comes first.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the sale stands even if he freed the slaves
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא quotes רבי יוחנן: the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, even when the first recipient freed עבדים in the property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, even if there were slaves in the property and he freed them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement adds a detail to the ruling of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, that what the first recipient does with the property stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first recipient's actions are valid even when he freed slaves that were part of the property. Once they are free, the second recipient cannot get them back.

keyTerms.meaning: The law follows the view of

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halakha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
and even if there were slaves among them
and he set them free.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the practical ruling of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and adds a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first recipient's actions are valid under רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, including freeing slaves in the property.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן needed to say this. If his actions stand, freeing slaves should stand too.
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions why the slave case needed to be stated. It sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first recipient may sell the property, freeing slaves seems to be just another way of giving it up. So the extra detail looks unnecessary.

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether step 14 teaches anything new.
steps.kashyaTarget: The added detail in רבי יוחנן's ruling about freeing slaves.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the first recipient's actions are valid, freeing slaves should obviously be valid as well.

steps.title: The giver didn't mean to permit something forbidden
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought the giver could say 'I didn't give them to you so you could do an איסור,' so the freeing would not count. רבי יוחנן teaches that it does count.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that the giver could tell him: 'I didn't give them to you to do something forbidden.' So he teaches us that it still works.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רבי יוחנן's detail adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Freeing an עבד כנעני is forbidden. So we might think the giver never let the first recipient use the slaves that way, and the freeing would not work. רבי יוחנן teaches that the freeing works even so.

keyTerms.meaning: He teaches us (that it is not so)

phrases.english: You might have said that he could tell him:
phrases.notes: The giver is speaking to the first recipient.

phrases.english: "To do something forbidden I did not give to you";
so he teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the case is not obvious by naming a reasonable mistaken assumption.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The giver did not intend to allow a forbidden act, so freeing the slaves would not work.
steps.terutzMaskana: The freeing works, and the second recipient cannot reclaim the freed slaves.
steps.whatToRemember: Under רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, as רבי יוחנן rules, the first recipient's actions stand, including freeing slaves in the property, even though freeing them is forbidden.

steps.title: The ruling holds even if the gift was made into shrouds
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes רבי יוחנן: the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, even if the first recipient turned the gift into shrouds for a dead person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, even if the first person made the items into shrouds for a dead person.
steps.whatsHappening: A second version of רבי יוחנן's ruling is brought. This time the example is shrouds for the dead instead of freeing עבדים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once cloth becomes shrouds for a dead person, nobody may get any benefit from it. So the second recipient loses it completely. רבי יוחנן says the first recipient's action still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Shrouds, the cloth a dead body is wrapped in

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef says that Rabbi Yochanan says:
The halacha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
even if he made them into shrouds for a dead person.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the gifted items. Once they are made into shrouds, no one may benefit from them, so the second person gets nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel version of the ruling in step 14, with a new example (shrouds instead of freeing עבדים).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first recipient's acts stand under רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, even making the property into forbidden shrouds.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן needed to say this.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling as unnecessary. If the first person's actions count, then making shrouds should count too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of question as step 15. If the first recipient really controls the property, any use he makes of it should stand. So why spell out this case?

keyTerms.meaning: It's obvious! (a challenge that a statement adds nothing new)

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether step 17 teaches anything new.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the first recipient's actions stand under רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, then making shrouds should obviously stand too, so the statement seems unnecessary.

steps.title: We might have thought the giver never agreed to make it forbidden
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought the giver could say 'I did not give you this so you could make it forbidden for benefit.' רבי יוחנן teaches that the act still counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that the giver can claim: 'I did not give them to you so you could turn them into things that are forbidden for benefit.' So he teaches us that it still counts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'obvious' question. There was a real reason to think shrouds might not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gift is given so the person can use and enjoy it. Turning it into something nobody may benefit from might seem to go against what the giver wanted. רבי יוחנן teaches that even so, the first recipient's act stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Things one may not get any benefit from
What might you have said (introduces the mistaken idea)

steps.whatToRemember: Under רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the first recipient's acts stand, whether he frees עבדים or makes shrouds. The giver cannot object that he didn't intend that use.

phrases.english: What might you have said?
To make them into things forbidden for benefit
I did not give them to you;
He teaches us (that it still counts).

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא לְשַׁוּוֹיִנְהוּ אִיסּוּרֵי הֲנָאָה לָא יְהַבִי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא (showing a reasonable mistaken idea that the statement corrects)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The giver could object that he never gave the items so they would become אסור בהנאה, so making shrouds would not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first recipient's act counts even though it makes the items forbidden for benefit.

steps.title: The אתרוג given 'to you, and after you to someone else'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא teaches: if someone gives an אתרוג as a gift 'to you, and after you to so-and-so,' and the first person uses it for the מצוה, this depends on the מחלוקת of רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא taught: if someone says 'This אתרוג is given to you as a gift, and after you to so-and-so,' and the first person took it and fulfilled his מצוה with it, this is the מחלוקת of רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching applies the 'after you' gift to an אתרוג. The question is whether the first person has fulfilled the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the first day of סוכות the אתרוג must belong to you. רב נחמן בר רב חסדא says it depends on how fully the first recipient owns it. That is the very point רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: The citron used for the מצוה on סוכות
He fulfilled his obligation with it

phrases.aramaic: דָּרַשׁ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Rav Chisda taught publicly:
"This etrog is given to you as a gift,
and after you, to so-and-so,"
the first one took it and fulfilled his obligation with it,
phrases.notes: The background assumption is that on the first day of סוכות your אתרוג has to be your own.

phrases.aramaic: בָּאנוּ לְמַחְלוֹקֶת רַבִּי וְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.
phrases.english: we have arrived at the dispute between Rabbi and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרַשׁ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic that applies the 'after you' gift to the מצוה of אתרוג.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether the first recipient of an 'after you' אתרוג fulfills the מצוה depends on the מחלוקת of רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: Their argument is only about owning the use of something
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק objects. רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only argue about whether owning the use of something is like owning the thing itself. He begins to explain why the אתרוג case is different.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק challenged this: רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only argue there because one holds that owning the use is like owning the thing itself, and the other holds it is not. But here...
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק attacks the claim that the אתרוג case depends on this מחלוקת. He pins down what the argument is really about, and starts to set up why the אתרוג is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to him, the whole מחלוקת is about one question: is owning the use of something the same as owning the thing itself? He is about to argue that the אתרוג case does not turn on that question. His explanation continues right after 'but here.'

keyTerms.meaning: Owning the use or produce of something
They only argue in this case (and no further)

steps.confusionAlert: The amud ends in the middle of the sentence at 'but here.' רב נחמן בר יצחק gives his full reason why the אתרוג case is different on the next amud.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak challenged it:
They only disagree

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי וְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הָתָם,
phrases.english: Rabbi and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the regular 'to you, and after you to so-and-so' gift case.

phrases.english: because one master holds:
owning the use is like owning the thing itself,
phrases.notes: This is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, which is why a sale by the first person stands.

phrases.english: and the other master holds:

phrases.aramaic: קִנְיַן פֵּירוֹת לָאו כְּקִנְיַן הַגּוּף דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: owning the use is not like owning the thing itself.
But here,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 20's claim that the אתרוג case depends on the מחלוקת of רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא's claim that the אתרוג case is the מחלוקת of רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their מחלוקת is only about whether קנין פירות equals קנין הגוף. The אתרוג case may not depend on that question, so it cannot simply be tied to their argument.
